steps.title: Valpolicella
steps.body: Valpolicella lies north of Verona, in valleys running down from the Lessini mountains. The Classico zone, around Fumane, Marano and Negrar, is the historic heart. Simple Valpolicella is light and cherry-fresh. Superiore has more alcohol and ageing.

steps.title: Amarone and Recioto
steps.body: For Amarone and Recioto, the best bunches are dried for about 100 to 120 days in airy lofts, fruttai, losing 30 to 40% of their weight. Recioto della Valpolicella ferments sweet. Amarone della Valpolicella, DOCG since 2010, ferments nearly dry, to 15 to 16% alcohol, with dried cherry, raisin, chocolate and spice. It ages at least two years.

options: From dried grapes fermented nearly dry
steps.explanation: Appassimento concentrates the grapes; fermentation runs almost dry.

steps.title: Ripasso
steps.body: Ripasso, re-passed, is Valpolicella refermented on the leftover skins of Amarone or Recioto, gaining body, colour and dried fruit flavour. It's sometimes called baby Amarone, sitting between simple Valpolicella and Amarone in weight and price.

steps.prompt: Which Valpolicella wines use dried grapes or their skins?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Amarone and Recioto use dried grapes: dry and sweet
Ripasso is refermented on Amarone skins
